land.text: all of Funan: the Mekong delta, the Cambodian south and the Gulf coast, 'annexed Funan' (Book of Sui, 636), 'in the beginning of the Zhenguan era (627–649)' (New Book of Tang)

successors.note: Chenla's own dossier (group se-01, other part) should carry the gain in 627; Cliopatria's Chenla shape grows from 184,000 to 427,000 km2 only in 641.

capitals.name: Vyadhapura (at or near Angkor Borei)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Vyadhapura'; 'Angkor Borei may have been Funan's premiere capital for much of that period'; the Angkor Borei page: 'This city was a settlement of the Kingdom of Funan and may have been its capital' (Takéo Province). Coordinates are Angkor Borei's (researcher's); Vyadhapura's site is not identified. The Chinese record has the king move south to 'Nafuna' after Chenla subjugated his city, undated.

keyframe_review.note: Years only: from 50 (infobox 'Establishment: 50 CE'; Cliopatria 51). 245,198 km2 covering the Mekong delta, the Cambodian south and the Gulf coast to the Chanthaburi hills: no infobox area to compare; 'parts of present-day Cambodia, Thailand and Vietnam' fits. The 2nd–3rd-century isthmus conquests are tributaries (vassal tint, ledger), not drawn as territory.

The same 245,198 km2 shape for 238–545: the pages opened record no border move; Fan Shiman's apex (reign 'A.D. 220–228' in the page's table), the Wu embassies of 228 and 243, the 270s joint attack on Tongking with Linyi and the embassies of 357–539 change no frontier.
Years only: 546–627. The shape is unchanged; Chenla's secession of 550 takes Champasak, which lies north of this shape, and the end is 627 (infobox 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE'), not 637.

correction.text: the 546 shape, which ends in 627; nothing is drawn for Funan in 638–640

keyframe_review.note: No Funan shape after 627: 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE' (infobox); the Book of Sui (636) already has Chenla 'annexed Funan'. The years 638–640 belong to Chenla.

region.text: the Mekong delta with Óc Eo and Angkor Borei 'linked by canals', the Cambodian south and the Gulf coast

ledger.note: 50: Funan established in the Mekong delta. Infobox 'Establishment: 50 CE'; Funan 'is believed to have been established in the 1st century CE'; the founder Hùntián (Kaundinya) and Soma are legend. Settlement at the sites goes back 'as far back as the 4th century BCE'; stateless land before (rule 8). Cliopatria begins 51; the boundary is Cliopatria's.

region.text: 'polities on the isthmus itself', the Malay peninsula's isthmus along the Gulf of Thailand

ledger.note: c. 220: Fan Shiman's conquests make the isthmus polities Funan's tributaries. 'Funan reached the apex of its power under the 3rd-century king Fan Shiman' (reign 'A.D. 220–228' in the page's table), who 'attacked more than ten kingdoms'; 'Funanese kings of the 2nd century conquered polities on the isthmus itself'. Vassal tint (rule 4); the Fan Shiman page would not load, so the polities' names (Dunsun and others) and exact years are missing; 220 is the reign's start.

region.text: Chenla's base, 'Champassak in about 550', with Vat Phou 'its spiritual center'

ledger.note: 550: Chenla breaks away. Chenla, 'a vassal of the Kingdom of Funan', 'whose base was Champassak in about 550, established their capital city at Isanapura (Sambhupura) by about 600'; infobox 'Vassal of Funan: 550' and the Funan infobox 'Chenla secession: 550'. Champasak lies north of Cliopatria's Funan shape, so the loss is of a dependency; no vassal_start is recorded because the page gives no year for the vassalage's start.

region.text: Funan's land north and west of the Mekong delta, attacked by Bhavavarman I and Citrasena from the end of the sixth century

ledger.note: c. 598: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena attack Funan. 'Chenla was recognized by a foreign power as a separate political entity at the end of the sixth century'; Bhavavarman I 'built a temple in 598'; the two 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627–649'. The start year is bridged from the temple date; blend (rule 6) over Funan's northern land until 627.

region.text: 'polities on the isthmus itself', the Malay peninsula's isthmus along the Gulf of Thailand

ledger.note: 627: the isthmus tributaries released at Funan's end. The page gives no end to their dependence on Funan; closed at the state's end.

region.text: Funan's land north and west of the Mekong delta, attacked by Bhavavarman I and Citrasena from the end of the sixth century

ledger.note: 627: the fighting ends in Chenla's favour. 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627–649'; Isanavarman's inscription at Īśānapura is 'dated 13 September 627 AD (K. 604)'.

627: Chenla annexes Funan. Infobox 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE'; the Book of Sui (636) says Chenla 'annexed Funan'; the New Book of Tang places it 'in the beginning of the Zhenguan era (627–649)'; the Chenla page: Funan, which 'had sent an embassy to China in 616 or 617', was subdued 'around 627–649'. The Chinese record has the king move south to 'Nafuna' after Chenla subjugated his city; Robert Nicholl's '680' collapse is a minority claim. Cliopatria keeps Funan to 640.

wars.name: Funan and Linyi attack Tongking (270s)
wars.outcome: 'In the 270s, Funan and Linyi jointly attacked Tongking', 'a brief conflict'; no border moved.
wars.note: Years 270–280 cover the page's '270s'; Cliopatria's 'Western Jin' row is the Jin of the 270s.

wars.name: Chenla's conquest of Funan (c. 598–627)

zones.text: Funan's land north and west of the Mekong delta, attacked by Bhavavarman I and Citrasena from the end of the sixth century

wars.outcome: Bhavavarman I and Citrasena Mahendravarman 'attacked Funan together and subdued it around 627–649'; Chenla 'annexed Funan' (Book of Sui, 636).
wars.note: The start year is bridged from Bhavavarman I's temple of 598; the page says only 'at the end of the sixth century'.

certainty.note: A mandala with no recorded frontier; the shape is Cliopatria's throughout, and the isthmus tributaries are a tint whose extent is the researcher's.

sources.title: Funan

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Funan' 51–640 (4 identical shapes) kept as one dossier; corrected to 50–627 from the infobox ('Establishment: 50 CE', 'Chenla conquest: 627 CE'); the 638–640 shape is wrong (Chenla's years). The four shapes are identical, so no border move needs explaining; the shape itself (245,198 km2) could not be checked against an infobox area because the page gives none, and the Seshat pages (kh_funan_1, kh_funan_2) were not opened.

Unsettled: the names and years of the isthmus tributaries (Dunsun and the others), because https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_Shiman and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fan_Shih-man would not load; the start of Chenla's vassalage (no page gives it, so only the 550 secession is in the ledger); the date of the court's move to 'Nafuna' (undated in the Chinese record); whether the conquest should be dated 627 (infobox), 'around 627–649' (Chenla page) or later; Robert Nicholl's 680 claim is ignored. Central Thailand (Chan Sen, Nakhon Pathom) is on the page as trade contact or 'Funan-related', not as territory; Dvaravati, which Cliopatria lacks, is for the group's additions batch.

Requests to other dossiers: chenla (se-01) should carry the 627 gain of all Funan and, if its agent finds a page, a vassal_start under Funan before 550; Cliopatria's Chenla shape jumps to 427,000 km2 in 641, fourteen years late. Gazetteer: 'Champasak', 'Southern Thailand', 'Mekong Delta' and 'Tonkin' resolve.
